anchor: Per-city signature data: demographics (% foreign-born, % foreign-owned firms), 3 signature sectors that characterise the city vs comparable metros (banks excluded — too generic), 6 cultural spectrum scores (1-10), and 5 government-and-institutions scores (0-10, business perspective). Curated per city; NYC ships first as the sample. Cultural spectrums are not 'good/bad', they are 'closer to one side', so the bar position tells the reader what the city's culture leans toward. Government scores are 0-10 where higher means better-for-business in all five dimensions.

convention.foreign_born_pct: Share of resident population that was not born in the country, 0-100
convention.foreign_owned_pct: Share of resident SMB firms with at least one foreign owner, 0-100
convention.signature_sectors: Three industries that characterise the city vs similar metros. NOT banks (too generic). Linked to industry slugs from the existing taxonomy.

culture.corruption_rejection: 1 = corruption widely tolerated, 10 = strongly rejected (matches the bar's low-left/high-right direction)

government.time_efficiency: 0 = months for any permit, 10 = same-day filing

commercial_streets.name: Fifth Avenue
commercial_streets.sells: Luxury flagship: Tiffany, Bergdorf Goodman, Saks, Apple Cube. The most expensive retail real estate in the world.

commercial_streets.name: Madison Avenue
commercial_streets.sells: Luxury designers, bespoke tailoring, contemporary art galleries. Quieter than 5th Ave, much more bespoke.

commercial_streets.name: SoHo
commercial_streets.sells: Brand flagships and contemporary fashion. Streetwear, denim, sneakers, beauty concept stores.

commercial_streets.name: Times Square and Broadway
commercial_streets.sells: Destination retail at scale: M&M, Disney, Hard Rock. Plus 41 theaters anchoring live entertainment.

commercial_streets.name: Garment District
commercial_streets.sells: Wholesale fabric, trim suppliers, showrooms, sample-makers. The B2B back-end of US fashion.

commercial_streets.name: Diamond District
commercial_streets.sells: Diamonds and jewelry, retail and wholesale. One of the most concentrated jewelry markets globally.

commercial_streets.name: Williamsburg (Bedford Avenue)
commercial_streets.sells: Independent fashion, craft goods, vintage, third-wave coffee. The reference market for hipster retail.

commercial_streets.name: Flatiron and Union Square
commercial_streets.sells: Modern lifestyle brands, tech-adjacent retail, the Greenmarket farmers market, and Eataly food hall.

commercial_streets.name: Canal Street and Chinatown
commercial_streets.sells: Asian groceries and fish markets, jewelry, Manhattan's densest food block. Hong Kong-style street commerce.

commercial_streets.name: Restaurant Row
commercial_streets.sells: Pre-theater restaurants. Italian, French, steakhouses concentrated for the Broadway crowd.

signature_sectors.label: Advertising and media
signature_sectors.blurb: Madison Avenue still anchors the global ad industry. Big networks, every major holding company, and a deep pool of creative agencies for film, print, and digital.

signature_sectors.label: Fashion and garment design
signature_sectors.blurb: Garment District plus New York Fashion Week make the metro the US capital for fashion design, sample-making, and showroom-driven wholesale.

signature_sectors.label: Broadway and live theater
signature_sectors.blurb: Forty-one theaters, 14.5 million annual tickets. The world's reference market for staged production: writers, casting, set, lighting, and the ecosystem around it.

new-york.notes: NYC-specific commercial-permit timelines drag time_efficiency; state + city taxes stack onto federal so the tax_predictability is moderate. Strong rule of law and very low bribery. Direct, ambitious culture as expected for the global archetype.
